original_question: Let Act(F∞,([0, 1], λ)) be the space of measure-preserving actions of F∞ on [0,1], and for x in this space let Sch(x) be the Schreier graph of the action on [0,1]. Is the set of x such that Sch(x) has a measurable perfect matching Σ1_1-complete?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost verbatim: it uses the same ambient action space Act(F∞,([0,1], λ)), the same notation Sch(x), the same property 'has a measurable perfect matching', and asks the same descriptive-set-theoretic complexity question, namely whether the corresponding set is Σ^1_1-complete.
missing_details: The paper first specifies that Aut([0,1], λ) is the space of automorphisms of Lebesgue measure on [0,1] equipped with the weak topology.
It then places Act(F∞,([0,1], λ)) as a closed subspace of Aut([0,1], λ)^{F∞}; this ambient Polish-space context should be made explicit if the question is to be fully stand-alone.
The actions under consideration are specifically actions of F∞ on [0,1] by automorphisms of Lebesgue measure, not merely arbitrary measure-preserving maps in an unspecified sense.
For full descriptive-set-theoretic precision, Σ^1_1-completeness should be understood for this subset of the Polish space Act(F∞,([0,1], λ)).
No additional hypotheses such as freeness, ergodicity, or amenability are part of Problem 42, so none should be added.

If one wants maximal stand-alone clarity, one may spell out standard notation that is left implicit in the paper, such as F∞ being the free group on countably many generators and Sch(x) being the Schreier graph associated to the action.
refined_question: Let Aut([0,1], λ) be the space of automorphisms of Lebesgue measure on [0,1], equipped with the weak topology, and let Act(F∞,([0,1], λ)) ⊆ Aut([0,1], λ)^{F∞} be the closed subspace consisting of actions of F∞ on [0,1] by such automorphisms. For x ∈ Act(F∞,([0,1], λ)), let Sch(x) denote the Schreier graph of the action on [0,1]. Is the set {x ∈ Act(F∞,([0,1], λ)) : Sch(x) has a measurable perfect matching} Σ^1_1-complete?
